report.summary: Two product defects account for all four failures, both visible in this run's app behavior: year validation accepts next year (year_off_by_one), and GET /api/books and the books page return every user's books (leak_books). Fix the owner filter in list_books and the year bound in validate_book first; that should clear all four tests. The workflow file does not set BUGS, so also confirm where this run's app got its BUGS setting.

causes.title: Books with next year's publication year are accepted instead of rejected
causes.explanation: validate_book uses max_year = this_year + 1 when the year_off_by_one bug flag is on, so a year one past the current year passes validation. The API returns 201 where the test expects 422, and the UI add form saves the book with no error shown. This is deterministic, so the tests are right to fail.
evidence: app/main.py:94: max_year = this_year + 1 if "year_off_by_one" in BUGS else this_year
app/main.py:95-96: if not 1 <= book.year <= max_year: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
UI failure: 'Expect to_contain_text get_by_test_id("error")' not found, and the aria snapshot shows row 'Future-75ccdf87 Someone 2027 Delete' was saved
causes.suggested_fix: Set max_year = this_year in validate_book and remove the year_off_by_one flag from the code path used by the tests (or make sure BUGS is not set for the test run).

causes.title: Book list is not filtered by owner, so users see each other's books
causes.explanation: With the leak_books flag on, list_books runs an unfiltered SELECT on the books table. Any user's list (API or page) then includes books owned by other users. The API test sees another user's book id in the list. The new-user page shows books from other tests, so the empty-state element never renders. This is deterministic, not a timing issue.
evidence: tests\api\test_books_api.py:42: assert book["id"] not in other_ids  ->  'assert 2 not in [1, 2]'
app/main.py:163-164: if "leak_books" in BUGS: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()

tests\ui\test_login_ui.py:14: expect(books.empty_state).to_be_visible() fails with 'element(s) not found'; aria snapshot lists rows 'Final title Someone 2001', 'From API-ba273c99 Robot', which belong to other users
app/main.py:30 template renders empty-state only when books is empty (app/templates/books.html:29-30)
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the leak_books branch in list_books so the query always filters by owner_id = ?. Then re-run the api and ui suites.
